9: Overview
10: --------
11: 
12: GNU Octave is a high-level interpreted language, primarily intended
13: for numerical computations.  It provides capabilities for the
14: numerical solution of linear and nonlinear problems, and for
15: performing other numerical experiments.  It also provides extensive
16: graphics capabilities for data visualization and manipulation.  GNU
17: Octave is normally used through its interactive interface (CLI and

19: The GNU Octave language is quite similar to Matlab so that most

35: 
36: Availability
37: ------------
38: 
39: The latest released version of Octave is always available from
40: <https://ftp.gnu.org/gnu/octave/> and many mirror sites around the
41: world.  You may also find links to binary distributions at
42: <https://www.octave.org/download.html>.  The current development
43: sources may be found under the Source Code tab on
44: [Savannah](https://savannah.gnu.org/projects/octave/).
45: 
46: You are encouraged to verify the Octave installation file you download
47: (such as `octave-11.1.0.tar.xz`) as follows:
48: * First, ensure that you are downloading from the official Octave website, or
49: from a GNU mirror linked from the official Octave website.
50: * Next, download the corresponding signature file for the installation file
51: you downloaded, for example `octave-11.1.0.tar.xz.sig`.
52: * Next, run the command
53: ```
54:   gpg --keyserver hkps://keys.gnupg.net --recv-keys B05F05B75D36644B
55: ```
56: to import John W. Eaton's public key (this needs to be done only once).
57: * Verify the integrity of the file you downloaded with a command like
58: ```
59:   gpg --verify octave-11.1.0.tar.xz.sig
60: ```
61: * If all is well, then the output should say
62: ```
63:   gpg: Good signature from "John W. Eaton <jwe@gnu.org>
64: ```
65: * If the file you downloaded was corrupted or changed by anyone else, then
66: the output will say
67: ```
68:   gpg: BAD signature from "John W. Eaton <jwe@gnu.org>"
69: ```
70: If so, you should not install Octave from that file, but should start over.
71: 
72: Installation
73: ------------
74: 
75: Building Octave from source requires approximately 475 MB of disk space (or
76: approximately 3.8 GB with debugging symbols).  Once installed, Octave uses
77: approximately 75 MB of disk space (or approximately 415 MB if shared libraries
78: are not built or binaries include debugging symbols).
79: 
80: To compile Octave, you will need a recent version of:
81: 
82: - [GNU Make](https://www.gnu.org/software/make/)
83: - [GNU G++](https://gcc.gnu.org/) or a different C++20 compiler
84: - [GNU Fortran](https://gcc.gnu.org/fortran/), a different Fortran 77 compiler,
85:   or [f2c](http://www.netlib.org/f2c/)
86: 
87: Octave's Makefiles use features of GNU Make that are not present in
88: other versions of make.  If you use `f2c`, you will need a script
89: like `fort77` that works like a normal Fortran compiler by combining
90: `f2c` with your C compiler in a single script.
91: 
92: See the file `INSTALL.OCTAVE` or the wiki at <https://wiki.octave.org/Building>
93: for more detailed installation instructions.
94: 
95: Bugs and Patches
96: ----------------
97: 
98: The files `BUGS` and `doc/interpreter/bugs.txi` explain the recommended
99: procedure for reporting bugs on the [bug tracker](https://bugs.octave.org)
100: or contributing patches; online resources are also available
101: [here](https://octave.org/support).
102: 
103: Documentation
104: -------------
105: 
106: * [Octave's manual](https://docs.octave.org/interpreter/) is a
107:   comprehensive user guide covering introductive and more advanced
108:   topics.
109: * [Octave's wiki](https://wiki.octave.org) is a user community page,
110:   covering various topics and answering [FAQ](https://wiki.octave.org/FAQ).
111: * [Octave's Doxygen](https://docs.octave.org/doxygen/) documentation
112:   explains the C++ class libraries.
113: 
114: If you notice omissions or inconsistencies in the documentation, please
115: report them at our bug tracker.  Specific suggestions for ways to improve
116: Octave and its documentation are always welcome.  Reports with patches are
117: even more welcome.

* If all is well, then the output should say
```
  gpg: Good signature from "John W. Eaton <jwe@gnu.org>
```
* If the file you downloaded was corrupted or changed by anyone else, then
the output will say
```
  gpg: BAD signature from "John W. Eaton <jwe@gnu.org>"
```
If so, you should not install Octave from that file, but should start over.

Installation
------------

Building Octave from source requires approximately 475 MB of disk space (or
approximately 3.8 GB with debugging symbols).  Once installed, Octave uses
approximately 75 MB of disk space (or approximately 415 MB if shared libraries
are not built or binaries include debugging symbols).

To compile Octave, you will need a recent version of:

- [GNU Make](https://www.gnu.org/software/make/)
- [GNU G++](https://gcc.gnu.org/) or a different C++20 compiler
- [GNU Fortran](https://gcc.gnu.org/fortran/), a different Fortran 77 compiler,
  or [f2c](http://www.netlib.org/f2c/)

Octave's Makefiles use features of GNU Make that are not present in
other versions of make.  If you use `f2c`, you will need a script
like `fort77` that works like a normal Fortran compiler by combining
`f2c` with your C compiler in a single script.

See the file `INSTALL.OCTAVE` or the wiki at <https://wiki.octave.org/Building>
for more detailed installation instructions.

Bugs and Patches
----------------

The files `BUGS` and `doc/interpreter/bugs.txi` explain the recommended
procedure for reporting bugs on the [bug tracker](https://bugs.octave.org)
or contributing patches; online resources are also available
[here](https://octave.org/support).

Documentation
-------------

* [Octave's manual](https://docs.octave.org/interpreter/) is a
  comprehensive user guide covering introductive and more advanced
  topics.
* [Octave's wiki](https://wiki.octave.org) is a user community page,
  covering various topics and answering [FAQ](https://wiki.octave.org/FAQ).
* [Octave's Doxygen](https://docs.octave.org/doxygen/) documentation
  explains the C++ class libraries.

If you notice omissions or inconsistencies in the documentation, please
report them at our bug tracker.  Specific suggestions for ways to improve
Octave and its documentation are always welcome.  Reports with patches are
even more welcome.

Additional Information
----------------------

The Octave website is <https://www.octave.org>, and there is a forum

## that are specific to this site.
OCTAVE_SET_DEFAULT([localarchlibdir],
  '${libexecdir}/octave/site/exec/${canonical_host_type}')

OCTAVE_SET_DEFAULT([localapiarchlibdir],
  '${libexecdir}/octave/${api_version}/site/exec/${canonical_host_type}')

OCTAVE_SET_DEFAULT([localoctfiledir],
  '${libdir}/octave/site/oct/${canonical_host_type}')

OCTAVE_SET_DEFAULT([localapioctfiledir],
  '${libdir}/octave/site/oct/${api_version}/${canonical_host_type}')

OCTAVE_SET_DEFAULT([localveroctfiledir],

OCTAVE_SET_DEFAULT([localfcnfiledir], '${datadir}/octave/site/m')

  '${datadir}/octave/site/${api_version}/m')

OCTAVE_SET_DEFAULT([localverfcnfiledir], '${datadir}/octave/${version}/site/m')

## Where to install extra files like NEWS and doc-cache.
OCTAVE_SET_DEFAULT([octetcdir], '${datadir}/octave/${version}/etc')

## Where to install the language files for the GUI.
OCTAVE_SET_DEFAULT([octlocaledir], '${datadir}/octave/${version}/locale')

OCTAVE_SET_DEFAULT([doc_cache_file], '${octetcdir}/doc-cache')

OCTAVE_SET_DEFAULT([texi_macros_file], '${octetcdir}/macros.texi')

OCTAVE_SET_DEFAULT([imagedir], '${datadir}/octave/${version}/imagelib')

## Where Octave will search for example data files shipped with distribution.
OCTAVE_SET_DEFAULT([octdatadir], '${datadir}/octave/${version}/data')

OCTAVE_SET_DEFAULT([octdocdir], '${datadir}/octave/${version}/doc')

OCTAVE_SET_DEFAULT([startupfiledir], '${fcnfiledir}/startup')
OCTAVE_SET_DEFAULT([localstartupfiledir], '${localfcnfiledir}/startup')

OCTAVE_SET_DEFAULT([localapipkgdir],
  '${datadir}/octave/site/${api_version}')

201: ## Where Octave will look for man and info files.
202: OCTAVE_SET_DEFAULT([man1dir], '${mandir}/man1')
203: OCTAVE_SET_DEFAULT([man1ext], '.1')
204: OCTAVE_SET_DEFAULT([infofile], '${infodir}/octave.info')
205: 
206: ### Check for programs used in building, installing, and running Octave.
207: 
208: ## Programs used in configuring Octave.
209: dnl Find pkg-config executable (sets $PKG_CONFIG)
210: PKG_PROG_PKG_CONFIG
211: ## And where we will install our own .pc files.
212: PKG_INSTALLDIR
213: AC_SUBST([liboctave_pkgconfigdir], [$pkgconfigdir])
214: AC_SUBST([liboctinterp_pkgconfigdir], [$pkgconfigdir])
215: AC_SUBST([liboctmex_pkgconfigdir], [$pkgconfigdir])
216: 
217: ## Programs used in configure and Makefiles.
218: AC_PROG_AWK
219: AC_PROG_GREP
220: AC_PROG_EGREP
221: OCTAVE_PROG_FIND
222: OCTAVE_PROG_PERL
223: 
224: ## Verify GNU Make present and its capabilities.
225: OCTAVE_PROG_GNUMAKE
226: 
227: ## Programs used to build parts of Octave.
228: OCTAVE_PROG_GPERF
229: 
230: OCTAVE_PROG_FLEX
231: AC_SUBST([LEX_OUTPUT_ROOT], [lex.octave_])
232: 
233: OCTAVE_PROG_BISON
234: 
235: OCTAVE_PROG_MAKEINFO
236: OCTAVE_PROG_TEXI2DVI
237: OCTAVE_PROG_TEXI2PDF
238: 
239: OCTAVE_PROG_TAR_REPRODUCIBLE
240: 
241: ## Programs used when installing Octave.
242: AC_PROG_LN_S
243: AC_PROG_MKDIR_P
244: 
245: AC_PROG_INSTALL
246: INSTALL_SCRIPT="${INSTALL}"
247: AC_SUBST(INSTALL_SCRIPT)
248: 
249: ## Programs used when running Octave.
250: OCTAVE_PROG_GHOSTSCRIPT
251: OCTAVE_PROG_GNUPLOT
252: OCTAVE_PROG_PAGER
253: OCTAVE_PROG_PYTHON
254: 
255: ## Programs used to generate icons file formats.
256: OCTAVE_PROG_ICOTOOL
257: OCTAVE_PROG_RSVG_CONVERT
258: AM_CONDITIONAL([AMCOND_HAVE_ICON_TOOLS],
259:   [test -n "$ICOTOOL" && test -n "$RSVG_CONVERT"])
260: 
261: ### Determine path separator.
262: 
263: sepchar=':'
264: AC_ARG_WITH([sepchar],
265:   [AS_HELP_STRING([--with-sepchar=<char>],
266:     [use <char> as the path separation character])])
267: case $with_sepchar in
268:   yes | "")
269:     case $host_os in
270:       mingw* | msdosmsvc)
271:         sepchar=';' ;;
272:     esac
273:   ;;
274:   no)
275:     AC_MSG_ERROR([You are required to define a path separation character])
276:     ;;
277:   *)
278:     sepchar=$with_sepchar
279:   ;;
280: esac
281: AC_SUBST(sepchar)
282: AC_DEFINE_UNQUOTED(SEPCHAR, ['$sepchar'],
283:   [Define this to be the path separator for your system, as a character constant.])
284: AC_DEFINE_UNQUOTED(SEPCHAR_STR, ["$sepchar"],
285:   [Define this to be the path separator for your system, as a string.])
286: 
287: ### Define the path to the shell on the host system.
288: dnl Most systems will ensure /bin/sh is the default shell so this can be safely
289: dnl ignored by almost everyone.  However, there are exceptions, such as
290: dnl Android, where this will need to be set.
291: SHELL_PATH=/bin/sh
292: AC_ARG_WITH([shell],
293:   [AS_HELP_STRING([--with-shell=SHELL],
294:     [use SHELL as the shell interpreter (default: /bin/sh)])])
295: case $with_shell in
296:   no)
297:     AC_MSG_ERROR([A shell interpreter is required])
298:   ;;
299:   yes | "")
300:   ;;
301:   *)
302:     SHELL_PATH=$with_shell
303:   ;;
304: esac
305: AC_DEFINE_UNQUOTED([SHELL_PATH], ["$SHELL_PATH"],
306:   [Define this to be the path to the shell command interpreter.])
307: 
308: ### Determine which C++ compiler to use (we expect to find g++ or clang++).
309: 
310: # AC_PROG_CXX attempts to find the compiler flags for activating support for
311: # C++11.  As of autoconf version 2.71, the source code that it uses for that
312: # test includes parts that are invalid in C++20.
313: # We are using AX_CXX_COMPILE_STDCXX to determine the potentially needed flags
314: # for the C++ version that Octave requires.  So, skip the (unnecessary and
315: # broken) test for C++11 in AC_PROG_CXX by setting the following (undocumented)
316: # flag:
317: ac_cv_prog_cxx_cxx11=""
318: AC_PROG_CXX
319: AC_PROG_CXXCPP
320: 
321: ## Ensure that the C++ compiler fully supports C++20.
322: ## Preferably with GNU extensions if flags are required.
323: AX_CXX_COMPILE_STDCXX(20, [], mandatory)
324: 
325: ENABLE_STD_PMR_POLYMORPHIC_ALLOCATOR=yes
326: AC_ARG_ENABLE(std-pmr-polymorphic-allocator,
327:   [AS_HELP_STRING([--disable-std-pmr-polymorphic-allocator],
328:                   [build libraries without support for std::pmr::polymorphic_allocator, less efficient transfer of arrays to external MEX files])],
329:   [case $enableval in
330:      yes) ENABLE_STD_PMR_POLYMORPHIC_ALLOCATOR=yes ;;
331:      no) ENABLE_STD_PMR_POLYMORPHIC_ALLOCATOR=no ;;
332:      *) AC_MSG_ERROR([bad value $enableval for --enable-std-pmr-polymorphic-allocator]) ;;
333:    esac])
334: 
335: AC_ARG_WITH([qt],
336:   [AS_HELP_STRING([--with-qt=VER], [use the Qt major version VER])
337: dnl Second help string must not be indented for correct alignment
338: AS_HELP_STRING([--without-qt], [don't use Qt libraries, disable Qt GUI])],
339:   [case $withval in
340:      yes | "")
341:      ;;
342:      no)
343:        QT_VERSIONS=
344:      ;;
345:      *)
346:        QT_VERSIONS="$withval"
347:      ;;
348:    esac])
349: 
350: ### Determine C++ compiler capabilities.
351: 
352: if test $ENABLE_STD_PMR_POLYMORPHIC_ALLOCATOR = yes; then
353:   OCTAVE_CHECK_STD_PMR_POLYMORPHIC_ALLOCATOR
354: else
355:   HAVE_STD_PMR_POLYMORPHIC_ALLOCATOR="no"
356: fi
357: 
358: ### Determine which C compiler to use (we expect to find gcc or clang).
359: 
360: AC_PROG_CC
361: AC_PROG_CPP
362: 
363: ## Save and restore CFLAGS and CXXFLAGS globally.
364: dnl These variables are for users, so we shouldn't be touching them.
365: dnl Instead, we should set the corresponding AM_ flags (currently by way of the
366: dnl XTRA_ variables).  However, for the duration of the configure script, we
367: dnl may set CFLAGS and CXXFLAGS so that subsequent tests succeed.  Temporary
368: dnl settings like this are currently done for pthreads and openmp, for example.
369: original_octave_configure_CFLAGS="$CFLAGS"
370: original_octave_configure_CXXFLAGS="$CXXFLAGS"
371: 
372: ## Check for MSVC
373: have_msvc=no
374: case $host_os in
375:   msdosmsvc)
376:     have_msvc=yes
377:   ;;
378:   mingw*)
379:     AC_MSG_CHECKING([for MSVC compiler])
380:     AC_PREPROC_IFELSE([AC_LANG_SOURCE([[
381:         #if ! defined (_MSC_VER)
382:         #error "Not MSVC compiler"
383:         #endif
384:         ]])],
385:       have_msvc=yes, have_msvc=no)
386:     AC_MSG_RESULT([$have_msvc])
387:   ;;
388: esac
389: 
390: ### gnulib initialization: part 1
391: dnl Must take place immediately after a compiler is determined
392: 
393: gl_EARLY
394: 
395: ### Record version number when using g++.
396: 
397: GXX_VERSION=
398: if test "$GXX" = yes; then
399:   AC_CACHE_CHECK([g++ compiler version number],
400:     [octave_cv_gxx_version],
401:     [octave_cv_gxx_version=[`$CXX -v 2>&1 | $GREP "^.*g.. version" | $SED -e 's/^.*g.. version *//' -e 's/cygnus-//' -e 's/egcs-//' -e 's/ .*//'`]
402:   ])
403: 
404:   GXX_VERSION=$octave_cv_gxx_version
405: fi
406: AC_SUBST(GXX_VERSION)
407: 
408: ### Record version number when using gcc.
409: dnl It might be different from the g++ version number.
410: 
411: GCC_VERSION=
412: if test "$GCC" = yes; then
413:   AC_CACHE_CHECK([gcc compiler version number],
414:     [octave_cv_gcc_version],
415:     [octave_cv_gcc_version=[`$CC -v 2>&1 | $GREP "^.*gcc version" | $SED -e 's/^.*g.. version *//' -e 's/cygnus-//' -e 's/egcs-//' -e 's/ .*//'`]
416:   ])
417: 
418:   GCC_VERSION=$octave_cv_gcc_version
419: fi
420: AC_SUBST(GCC_VERSION)
421: 
422: ## It seems that there are some broken inline assembly functions in GNU libc.
423: ## Since it is uncertain how to test whether Octave is linked against GNU libc,
424: ## just disable them for all platforms.
425: 
426: AC_MSG_NOTICE([defining __NO_MATH_INLINES avoids buggy GNU libc exp function])
427: AC_DEFINE(__NO_MATH_INLINES, 1,
428:   [Define to 1 if your version of GNU libc has buggy inline assembly code for math functions like exp.])
429: 
430: ### Determine the compiler flag necessary to create dependencies.
431: 
432: ## Assume GCC.
433: INCLUDE_DEPS=yes
434: DEPEND_FLAGS="-M"
435: DEPEND_EXTRA_SED_PATTERN=""
436: if test "$GCC" != yes; then
437:   case $canonical_host_type in
438:     sparc-sun-solaris2* | i386-pc-solaris2*)
439:       DEPEND_FLAGS="-xM1"
440:       DEPEND_EXTRA_SED_PATTERN="-e '/\/opt\/SUNWspro/d'"
441:     ;;
442:     *-*-msdosmsvc)
443:     ;;
444:     *-*-mingw*)
445:       if test $have_msvc = no; then
446:         INCLUDE_DEPS=no
447:       fi
448:     ;;
449:     *)
450:       INCLUDE_DEPS=no
451:     ;;
452:   esac
453: fi
454: AC_SUBST(INCLUDE_DEPS)
455: AC_SUBST(DEPEND_FLAGS)
456: AC_SUBST(DEPEND_EXTRA_SED_PATTERN)
457: 
458: ### Check for math library.
459: dnl If found, this will add -lm to LIBS.
460: 
461: dnl Keep this check before the check for the Fortran compiler,
462: dnl in case -lm is needed to compile Fortran programs.
463: AC_CHECK_LIB(m, sin)
464: 
465: ### Determine the Fortran compiler and how to invoke it.
466: 
467: ## Prefer gfortran, but the user's F77 environment variable will override.
468: AC_PROG_F77([gfortran])
469: if test -z "$F77"; then
470:   ## No gfortran found, search for any other installed compiler.
471:   AC_PROG_F77
472: fi
473: if test "$F77" = g77; then
474:   AC_MSG_ERROR([g77 is not a supported Fortran compiler.  Select another compiler by setting the environment variable F77 and re-running configure.])
475: fi
476: 
477: AC_MSG_CHECKING([whether a usable Fortran compiler was found])
478: if test -n "$F77"; then
479:   AC_MSG_RESULT(yes)
480: else
481:   AC_MSG_RESULT(no)
482:   AC_MSG_ERROR([a Fortran compiler is required to build Octave])
483: fi
484: 
485: AC_F77_LIBRARY_LDFLAGS
486: AC_F77_DUMMY_MAIN
487: AC_F77_WRAPPERS
488: 
489: ## Must appear after checks for Fortran compiler.
490: OCTAVE_CHECK_FORTRAN_SYMBOL_AND_CALLING_CONVENTIONS
491: 
492: ## Must appear after checks for all compilers.
493: OCTAVE_DEFINE_MKOCTFILE_DYNAMIC_LINK_OPTIONS
494: 
495: ### Use a 64-bit integer type for array dimensions and indexing, if possible.
496: 
497: AC_CHECK_SIZEOF([int])
498: AC_DEFINE_UNQUOTED(OCTAVE_SIZEOF_INT, [$ac_cv_sizeof_int],
499:   [Define to the size of int.])
500: 
501: AC_CHECK_SIZEOF([void *])
502: if test $ac_cv_sizeof_void_p -ge 8; then
503:   ENABLE_64=yes
504: else
505:   ENABLE_64=no
506: fi
507: 
508: AC_ARG_ENABLE(64,
509:   [AS_HELP_STRING([--disable-64],
510:     [don't use 64-bit integers for array dimensions and indexing])],
511:   [case $enableval in
512:      yes) ENABLE_64=yes ;;
513:      no) ENABLE_64=no ;;
514:      *) AC_MSG_ERROR([bad value $enableval for --enable-64]) ;;
515:    esac])

        AC_MSG_NOTICE([adding -mieee-fp to XTRA_CXXFLAGS])])

      OCTAVE_CC_FLAG([-mieee], [
        ieee_fp_flag=-mieee
        XTRA_CFLAGS="$XTRA_CFLAGS -mieee"

    else
      OCTAVE_CC_FLAG([-ieee], [
        ieee_fp_flag=-ieee
        XTRA_CFLAGS="$XTRA_CFLAGS -ieee"
        AC_MSG_NOTICE([adding -ieee to XTRA_CFLAGS])])
    fi
    if test "$GXX" = yes; then
      OCTAVE_CXX_FLAG([-mieee], [
        ieee_fp_flag=-mieee
        XTRA_CXXFLAGS="$XTRA_CXXFLAGS -mieee"
        AC_MSG_NOTICE([adding -mieee to XTRA_CXXFLAGS])])
    else
      OCTAVE_CXX_FLAG([-ieee], [

OCTAVE_CC_FLAG([-fexceptions], [
  CFLAGS="$CFLAGS -fexceptions"
  XTRA_CFLAGS="$XTRA_CFLAGS -fexceptions"

### Defaults for cross compiling.
dnl BUILD_CC and BUILD_CXX are the compilers that we use for building tools
dnl on the build system.  For now, we assume that the only cross compiling we
dnl can do is with gcc on a Unixy system, but the dedicated hacker can
dnl override these.

if test "$cross_compiling" = yes; then
  BUILD_CC="gcc"
  BUILD_CFLAGS="-O2 -g"
  BUILD_CXX="g++ -std=gnu++17"
  BUILD_CXXFLAGS="-O2 -g"
  BUILD_LDFLAGS=""

else
  BUILD_CC="${CC}"
  BUILD_CFLAGS="${CFLAGS}"
  BUILD_CXX="${CXX}"
  BUILD_CXXFLAGS="${CXXFLAGS}"
  BUILD_LDFLAGS="${LDFLAGS}"
  BUILD_EXEEXT="${EXEEXT}"
fi

AC_ARG_VAR([BUILD_CC],
  [build system C compiler (used if cross compiling)])
AC_ARG_VAR([BUILD_CFLAGS],

AC_ARG_VAR([BUILD_CXX],
  [build system C++ compiler (used if cross compiling)])
AC_ARG_VAR([BUILD_CXXFLAGS],
  [build system C++ compiler flags (used if cross compiling)])
AC_ARG_VAR([BUILD_LDFLAGS],
  [build system C++ compiler link flags (used if cross compiling)])
AC_ARG_VAR([BUILD_EXEEXT],
  [build system executable extension (used if cross compiling)])

### Determine whether to create cross-mkoctfile and other cross-tools.

cross_tools=no
AC_ARG_ENABLE([cross-tools],
  [AS_HELP_STRING([--enable-cross-tools],
    [build cross tools (mkoctfile, octave-config) if cross compiling])],
  [if test "$enableval" = yes; then cross_tools=yes; fi])

if test "$cross_tools" = yes; then
  if test "$cross_compiling" = no; then
    AC_MSG_WARN([ignoring --enable-cross-tools when not cross compiling])
    cross_tools=no
  fi
fi
AM_CONDITIONAL([AMCOND_CROSS_TOOLS], [test $cross_tools = yes])

  octave_save_CPPFLAGS="$CPPFLAGS"

  for element in $octave_save_CPPFLAGS; do
    octave_have_CPPFLAG=no
    for inc_element in $INCICONV; do
      if test "x$element" = "x$inc_element"; then

### Check for either of GraphicsMagick++/ImageMagick++ libraries.

check_magick=yes
use_magick=no
AC_ARG_WITH([magick],
  [AS_HELP_STRING([--with-magick=LIB],
    [select library to use for image I/O (options: GraphicsMagick++ (default) or ImageMagick++)])
dnl Second help string must not be indented for correct alignment
AS_HELP_STRING([--without-magick], [don't use Magick library, disable imread, imwrite, imformats, imfinfo])],
  [case $withval in
     yes | "")
       magick="GraphicsMagick++"
     ;;
     no)
       check_magick=no
     ;;
     *)
       magick="$withval"
     ;;
   esac],
  [magick="GraphicsMagick++"])

if test $check_magick = yes; then

  MAGICK_CPPFLAGS=
  MAGICK_LDFLAGS=
  MAGICK_LIBS=

  PKG_CHECK_EXISTS([$magick], [
    dnl We are using --cflags now instead of --cflags-only-I because some
    dnl Graphics/ImageMagick++ packages will provide -D options for
    dnl MAGICKCORE_HDRI_ENABLE and MAGICKCORE_QUANTUM_DEPTH that are needed
    dnl for building with a particular verison of the library.  If there
    dnl are other flags in the output from pkg-config --cflags that cause
    dnl trouble, then we may need to go back to using --cflags-only-I and
    dnl have a configure test to determine the proper definitions of
    dnl MAGICKCORE_HDRI_ENABLE and MAGICKCORE_QUANTUM_DEPTH.
    dnl See also bug #49563.
    MAGICK_CPPFLAGS="$($PKG_CONFIG --cflags $magick | $SED -e 's/^ *$//')"
    MAGICK_LDFLAGS="$($PKG_CONFIG --libs-only-L $magick | $SED -e 's/^ *$//')"
    MAGICK_LIBS="$($PKG_CONFIG --libs-only-l $magick | $SED -e 's/^ *$//')"

    warn_magick="$magick library fails tests.  The imread, imwrite, and imfinfo functions for reading and writing image files will not be fully functional."

    save_CPPFLAGS="$CPPFLAGS"
    save_LIBS="$LIBS"
    CPPFLAGS="$MAGICK_CPPFLAGS $CPPFLAGS"
    LIBS="$MAGICK_LDFLAGS $MAGICK_LIBS $LIBS"
    AC_LANG_PUSH(C++)
    AC_CHECK_HEADER([Magick++.h], [
      AC_CACHE_CHECK([for Magick::ColorRGB and Magick::PixelPacket in Magick++.h],
        [octave_cv_func_magick],
        [AC_LINK_IFELSE([AC_LANG_PROGRAM([[
          #include <Magick++.h>
          ]], [[
          Magick::ColorRGB c;
          Magick::PixelPacket pix;
          ]])],
          octave_cv_func_magick=yes,
          octave_cv_func_magick=no)
        ])
      if test $octave_cv_func_magick = yes; then
        use_magick=yes
        warn_magick=
      fi
    ])
    AC_LANG_POP(C++)
    CPPFLAGS="$save_CPPFLAGS"
    LIBS="$save_LIBS"
  ],
  [use_magick=no
   warn_magick="$magick library not found.  The imread, imwrite, and imfinfo functions for reading and writing image files will not be fully functional."])
fi

if test $use_magick = yes; then
  AC_DEFINE(HAVE_MAGICK, 1,
    [Define to 1 if Graphics/ImageMagick++ is available.])
else
  if test -n "$warn_magick"; then
    OCTAVE_CONFIGURE_WARNING([warn_magick])
  fi
  MAGICK_CPPFLAGS=
  MAGICK_LDFLAGS=
  MAGICK_LIBS=
fi
AC_SUBST(MAGICK_CPPFLAGS)
AC_SUBST(MAGICK_LDFLAGS)
AC_SUBST(MAGICK_LIBS)

if test $check_fltk = yes; then

      FLTK_CONFIG="$fltk_exec_prefix/bin/fltk-config"
    fi
  fi

  if test "x$fltk_prefix" != x; then
    fltk_args="$fltk_args --prefix=$fltk_prefix"
    if test x${FLTK_CONFIG+set} != xset ; then
      FLTK_CONFIG="$fltk_prefix/bin/fltk-config"
    fi
  fi

  AC_PATH_PROG([FLTK_CONFIG], [fltk-config], [no])

  warn_fltk_config=
  warn_fltk_opengl=

  if test "$FLTK_CONFIG" = no; then
    warn_fltk_config="FLTK config script not found.  FLTK toolkit will be disabled."
    OCTAVE_CONFIGURE_WARNING([warn_fltk_config])
  else
    ## Only include -I options in FLTK_CPPFLAGS
    fltk_cflags=`$FLTK_CONFIG $fltkconf_args --use-gl --cflags`
    for fltk_option in $fltk_cflags; do
      case $fltk_option in
        -I*)
          FLTK_CPPFLAGS="$FLTK_CPPFLAGS $fltk_option"
        ;;
      esac
    done
    FLTK_CPPFLAGS=`echo "$FLTK_CPPFLAGS" | $SED -e 's/^ \+//'`

    ## Split -L and -l options into FLTK_LDFLAGS and FLTK_LIBS
    fltk_ldflags=`$FLTK_CONFIG $fltkconf_args --use-gl --ldflags`
    for fltk_option in $fltk_ldflags; do
      case $fltk_option in
        -l*)
          FLTK_LIBS="$FLTK_LIBS $fltk_option"
        ;;
        *)
          FLTK_LDFLAGS="$FLTK_LDFLAGS $fltk_option"
        ;;
      esac
    done
    FLTK_LIBS=`echo "$FLTK_LIBS" | $SED -e 's/^ \+//'`
    FLTK_LDFLAGS=`echo "$FLTK_LDFLAGS" | $SED -e 's/^ \+//'`

    case $host_os in
      mingw*)
        FLTK_LDFLAGS=`echo $FLTK_LDFLAGS | $SED -e 's/-mwindows//g'`

    esac
    AC_LANG_PUSH(C++)
    AC_CACHE_CHECK([for OpenGL support in FLTK],
      [octave_cv_fltk_opengl_support],
      [save_CPPFLAGS="$CPPFLAGS"
      CPPFLAGS="$CFLAGS $FLTK_CPPFLAGS"
      AC_COMPILE_IFELSE([AC_LANG_PROGRAM([[

    if test $octave_cv_fltk_opengl_support = no; then
      warn_fltk_opengl="FLTK does not have OpenGL support.  OpenGL graphics with FLTK widgets will be disabled."
    else
      build_fltk_graphics=yes
      AC_DEFINE(HAVE_FLTK, 1, [Define to 1 if FLTK is available.])
    fi
    AC_LANG_POP(C++)

    if test -n "$warn_fltk_opengl"; then
      OCTAVE_CONFIGURE_WARNING([warn_fltk_opengl])
    fi
  fi
